The beta 6 of macOS 27 Golden Gate released today includes a brand new Golden Gate Bridge dynamic wallpaper, bringing the total number of dynamic wallpapers to five. Download links for all of them are provided below.

macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpaper gallery continues to expand

When Apple announced macOS 27 Golden Gate at WWDC26, it showed a unified system wallpaper across all operating systems featuring a stylized "27" number.

However, after a few developer betas, Apple began adding dynamic screensavers that double as wallpapers, showing slow-motion scenic views overlooking the famous San Francisco landmark, the Golden Gate Bridge.

After the Mac is unlocked, the screensaver will gradually come to a stop, leaving behind a fresh, slightly different wallpaper each time.

Although the dynamic effects are handled by macOS, a static screenshot gallery for each video clip is provided below, including frames from four videos, as well as light and dark versions of the unified stylized "27" wallpaper.

Remember to click on the images and save the full-resolution versions. To set them as your background, go to System Settings > Wallpaper, scroll down to "Your Photos," click the "Add Photo" button, then do any of the following:

Add photos from the Photos library: click "Choose from Photos," then select a photo. Add an image file: click "Choose File," pick a file, then click "Open." You can also drag images from your desktop or a folder onto the thumbnail at the top of the Wallpaper settings. Add a folder from Finder: click "Choose Folder," pick a folder, then click "Open." Add an album or folder from the Photos app: under "Photo Collections," pick an album or folder.

According to Apple, "You can also select a custom wallpaper without opening the Wallpaper settings":

Use photos from the Photos library: open the Photos app, select a photo, click the share button in the Photos toolbar, then click "Set as Wallpaper." Use an image found online: in the Safari window, Ctrl-click the image, then choose "Use Image as Desktop Wallpaper." Use images stored on your Mac: click Finder in the Dock to open a Finder window. Ctrl-click the image file, then click "Set Desktop Picture."

To learn more about setting custom wallpapers in macOS, click this link.

Have a favorite? Let us know in the comments.
